text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Cold spell begins to hit fuel prices, agriculture, public works and transports.
-- Financial markets unaffected by choice of two new members at the Bank of France monetary policy council, as see reshuffle not putting in jeopardy the franc's stability against the mark.
-- Bank Paribas reshuffles branch network, plans to open business center in Paris to boost activity.
-- Generale des Eaux sold 19 billion franc worth of assets in 1996.
-- State-owned bank Caisse des Depots forecasts a 0.44 percent growth of GDP for the first quarter of 1997.
-- Senate president Rene Monory criticises choice of Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard for the Bank of France monetary policy council, calls for changes to the nomination process.
-- State hopes to earn some 27 billion francs from planned 1997 privatisations, the largest of which is France Telecom's privatisation, scheduled for April.
-- Sanofi pharmaceutical firm to seek an alliance with a chemicals group in 1997. Chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq expects 1996 results to be in line with a forecast 10 percent profit growth .
-- Finance minister Jean Arthuis says he expects the two new members of Bank of France monetary policy council will favour a stable franc.
-- Social security fund CNAM addresses doctors to try and draw an agreement after failure of negotiations with doctors' unions.
-- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl predicts standoff over NATO's expansion into Eastern Europe will end this year.
